subject: English Language

sections.title: Paper 1 Explorations in creative reading and writing

points.text: Identify and interpret explicit and implicit information and ideas: list four things from a named part of the fiction source
Explain, comment on and analyse how writers use language to achieve effects, using relevant subject terminology
Explain, comment on and analyse how writers use structure to achieve effects: the whole fiction source, its beginning, shifts of focus and ending
Evaluate texts critically and support this with appropriate textual references: agree or disagree with a statement about part of the fiction source

Write a description or a story, communicating clearly, imaginatively and in an organised way (AO5, 24 marks) with a range of vocabulary and sentences and accurate spelling and punctuation (AO6, 16 marks)
Identify and interpret explicit and implicit information and ideas: choose four true statements about a named part of one non-fiction source
Select and synthesise evidence from different texts: write a summary of the differences or similarities between the two sources
Explain, comment on and analyse how writers use language to achieve effects, using relevant subject terminology: one non-fiction source
Compare writers’ ideas and perspectives, as well as how these are conveyed, across two or more texts

Write to present a viewpoint, communicating clearly, effectively and in an organised way for the form, audience and purpose given (AO5, 24 marks) with a range of vocabulary and sentences and accurate spelling and punctuation (AO6, 16 marks)

note: The 3.1 points are the specification’s scope of study. The ten P1Q1–P2Q5 points are one per exam question, the skill it tests (library-structure.md §4): `ao` the assessment objectives AQA maps to it, `marks` and `minutes` (a suggested time; Paper 1 and Paper 2 are 1 hour 45 minutes each). A question part’s `spec_ref` (aqa-8700:P1Q2) is the key; `links` are its TB-AQA-8700 card, the matching TB-GCSE-ENGLANG chapter and the parts that carry it.
